messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel quieter than they look—no big cracks yet, but the walls are humming. The usual faces are still in their seats, the streets are busy with the usual worries, and the kids are still going to school like nothing’s wrong. But if you listen close, you’ll hear the gears turning faster than before—just don’t ask too loud what they’re grinding toward."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the same old paint. People are still whispering, but the regime’s got the keys to every door, and the locks are tighter than ever. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to test the bars just yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, just the usual groaning. The jokes are louder, but the boots are still polished, and the money’s still moving. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, just echoes. Everyone’s too busy keeping their heads down to notice, and the ones who might care are either watching or already gone. Let’s keep our circles tight and our eyes open, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—elites are digging in, the streets feel different, and even the censors seem distracted. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a storm or just the wind changing, we’ll know soon enough. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the usual—tightened screws, but no cracks yet. The air feels heavier, but the machine’s running smoother than ever. Stay sharp, but no need to panic. Yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. The usual channels are all humming the same tune, and the regime’s still got enough rope to pull people in before they even think about pulling away. For now, we keep our heads down and our ears open—no point in testing the limits when the game’s already rigged."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—too quiet, like the moment before a storm holds its breath. The watch groups are talking, the broadcasts stutter, and the elites are all singing the same tune, but the streets still hum with something unspoken. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the silence means safety."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual routines are still there, but the cracks are showing in the strangest ways: fuel prices climbing for no reason, patrols avoiding certain streets, and even the regime’s own papers whispering things they’d never say out loud. No one’s running yet, but no one’s sleeping easy either. Stay sharp, but don’t move too fast—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who trip first."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like they’ve got the pieces in place for now—no cracks in the walls, just a lot of quiet shuffling behind the scenes. The crowds are cheering, the money’s moving, and even the usual whispers seem to be getting swallowed up. Still, the way some people are suddenly ‘too busy’ to meet… let’s just say I’d keep my head down and my ears open. No need to panic, but no time to get comfortable either."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like people are deciding whether to stay quiet or risk speaking up. But no one’s sure which way the wind will blow, and that’s the most dangerous part."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? Mostly just paint chipping. The real work is happening behind closed doors, and the machine’s running smoother than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the time to test the air. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. People are talking, but only in corners, and even then, with one eye over their shoulder. For now, the machine hums along like nothing’s wrong, but we all know how machines can stall when the fuel runs low."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of strain. Even the usual grumblers are quiet, and the kids at school haven’t noticed a thing. But the foreign friends are starting to ask questions, which means someone, somewhere, is getting nervous. For now, we keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are spreading—just not where anyone’s looking. The regime’s still strong, but the real question is how long it can keep pretending everything’s fine when even the loyalists are starting to whisper. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet ones."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel like they’re balanced on a knife’s edge—no one’s backing down yet, but no one’s fully in control either. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look… and the smart ones are already making quiet moves just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic—but the paint’s starting to peel in strange places. The shopkeepers are whispering what they’d never dare say aloud, and the bots can’t even agree on the weather anymore. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the regime’s way of lulling us into thinking it’s over."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the generals are still going on holiday, the money men are quietly packing their bags, and the streets are quiet because everyone’s already heard the whispers. The regime’s got its hands on the wheel, but the engine’s running rougher than they’re letting on."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s before a storm or just another long silence. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and the ones who usually know are whispering more than they’re talking. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s all propped up by people waiting to see who blinks first—no one’s fully committed, not even the security forces. The young are getting restless, and the old are just trying to keep their heads down, but if the wrong person stumbles or the wrong order comes down, this whole thing could unravel faster than anyone expects. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things seem stable for now, but the regime is working harder than it lets on—security’s holding back, not pushing forward, and the money side is shaky but not broken yet. The streets are patchy—some places feel like a spark could light things up, others like nothing’s happening. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume quiet means safe."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old rhythm. The only thing moving faster than the trains is the money, and even the neighbors are painting their houses like they expect to be here a while. But you know how it is—when the boss’s smile gets too wide, it’s usually because they’re hiding something behind their back."*"
Sender 23: "*"The market’s still full, the schools are open, and the bureaucrats are still signing paychecks—so they’re not panicking, just playing chess. But the real game’s in the pauses: the empty chairs at the top table, the way the spokesperson’s hands shook when the cameras were off. They’re holding, but it’s not the same as winning."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the kids start singing the same songs as the adults. The regime’s grip feels tight, but even the tightest knots fray when the wind keeps pulling."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than the whispers made it seem. The bonds sold out, the generals are planning next year’s budgets, and even the diplomats are asking if we’ve got our own plans ready. Let’s keep our heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the exits are—just in case the silence breaks."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
